Forbidden heaps and the spectral solution of free-fermion-in-disguise circuits

Istvan Vona

10 November 2026

Download PDFLaTeX source Paper + code bundle

Abstract

The spectrum of a free-fermion-in-disguise (FFD) circuit can depend on the order of its gates, even when every local gate is unchanged. We classify the open, one-pass palindromic circuits whose canonical transfer polynomial has commuting coefficients and central inversion. Commuting gate exchanges reduce a permutation to a heap: the relative order of every noncommuting pair. The criterion is local. A heap is admissible precisely when it avoids twenty orientations of a single six-vertex graph, or five patterns up to reflection and reversal. The transfer polynomial follows directly from the circuit expansion, with a binary-nullity grading that counts temporal overlaps rather than selected gates. Its generic spectrum is obtained from polynomial roots, with central-sector sign constraints stated explicitly. A bounded-frontier algorithm computes the required sector polynomials without constructing the many-body matrices. The all-length proof combines a local obstruction, a triangle-interlacement reduction, and exact finite certificates. Complete proofs, pseudocode, and a reproducible verification record are supplied below. The necessity statement concerns this canonical transfer construction, not every conceivable free-fermion representation.

The ordering problem.#

Free fermions in disguise have a factorized many-body spectrum without an evident Jordan–Wigner reduction of their local spin operators [1, 2]. For quantum circuits, free-fermion solvability is sensitive to the arrangement of the gates. Pozsgay and Fukai posed this ordering problem [3]; Szász-Schagrin, Cristani, Piroli, and Vernier subsequently constructed transfer matrices and polynomial-root solutions for three staircase and brickwork families, conventionally called I, II, and III [4].

Here we treat an arbitrary permutation within a fixed class of palindromes. The result has two parts: a finite forbidden-pattern criterion for the canonical transfer family, and an explicit spectral solution for every accepted heap. Neither translation invariance nor a repeating circuit architecture is required.

The open FFD algebra is generated by Hermitian involutions satisfying

hj2=1,hj⁢hk={−hk⁢hj,1≤|j−k|≤2,hk⁢hj,|j−k|>2.h_{j}^{2}=1,\quad h_{j}h_{k}=\begin{cases}-h_{k}h_{j},&1\leq|j-k|\leq 2,\\ h_{k}h_{j},&|j-k|>2.\end{cases} (1)

With uj=exp⁡(i⁢ϕj⁢hj/2)u_{j}=\exp(i\phi_{j}h_{j}/2) and a permutation π\pi of [M][M], set

Gπ=uπ1⁢⋯⁢uπM,Vπ=Gπ⁢GπT.G_{\pi}=u_{\pi_{1}}\cdots u_{\pi_{M}},\qquad V_{\pi}=G_{\pi}G_{\pi}^{T}. (2)

Here TT reverses products and fixes each hjh_{j} and the scalar ii; it is not the adjoint. Thus the second half retraces the first, with the same angles.

A heap forgets only irrelevant ordering.#

Draw an edge between labels at distance one or two, obtaining the graph FM=PM2F_{M}=P_{M}^{2}. Direct each edge from the gate appearing earlier in the half-word to the gate appearing later. This acyclic orientation is the heap DD. Its transitive closure is a partial order; its linear extensions are exactly the words related by adjacent exchanges of commuting gates [5]. All those words give the same circuit. Figure 1 illustrates the distinction between the spatial graph and its temporal ordering.

The canonical transfer polynomial.#

Write xj=cos⁡ϕjx_{j}=\cos\phi_{j} and yj=sin⁡ϕjy_{j}=\sin\phi_{j}. For a selected set SS, let eD⁢(v,S)e_{D}(v,S) be the parity of its selected out-neighbors. The set is feasible when eD⁢(v,S)=0e_{D}(v,S)=0 at every selected vertex. Peeling the palindrome from its outside gives the exact expansion

where HD⁢(S)H_{D}(S) is the product of the selected generators in temporal order.

The nontrivial step is assigning a spectral degree. In temporal coordinates on SS, let Na⁢b=1N_{ab}=1 when a<ba<b and the corresponding generators anticommute. Work over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2} and define

KD⁢(S)\displaystyle K_{D}(S) =offdiag⁡[(I+N)T⁢(I+N)],\displaystyle=\operatorname{offdiag}[(I+N)^{T}(I+N)], (5)

A column of I+NI+N marks an event together with its earlier selected neighbors. Thus KK records the pairwise overlaps of these predecessor footprints, excluding self-overlap. This is not a gate count: a feasible three-gate temporal fork has ν=1\nu=1.

The canonical polynomial is

𝖠D(z)=∑S⁢ feasibleaD(S)zνD⁢(S)HD(S).\boxed{\mathsf{A}_{D}(z)=\sum_{S\text{ feasible}}a_{D}(S)z^{\nu_{D}(S)}H_{D}(S% ).} (6)

It obeys 𝖠D⁢(1)=VD\mathsf{A}_{D}(1)=V_{D}, 𝖠D⁢(0)=a0⁢𝟏\mathsf{A}_{D}(0)=a_{0}\mathbf{1} with a0=∏jxja_{0}=\prod_{j}x_{j}, and 𝖠D⁢(z)†=𝖠D⁢(−z)\mathsf{A}_{D}(z)^{\dagger}=\mathsf{A}_{D}(-z) for real zz.

The local classification.#

The obstruction graph HH has two triangles sharing an edge and a pendant edge at each end:

E⁢(H)={A⁢B,B⁢C,B⁢D,C⁢D,C⁢E,D⁢E,E⁢F}.E(H)=\{AB,BC,BD,CD,CE,DE,EF\}. (7)

Its relevant copies occupy

(A,B,C,D,E,F)=(a,a+2,a+3,a+4,a+5,a+7).(A,B,C,D,E,F)=(a,a+2,a+3,a+4,a+5,a+7). (8)

Orient the edges by any one of the five words

ADBCFE,ADBCEF,ACBFED,ACBDFE,ACBDEF.\begin{gathered}\texttt{ADBCFE},\quad\texttt{ADBCEF},\quad\texttt{ACBFED},\\ \texttt{ACBDFE},\quad\texttt{ACBDEF}.\end{gathered} (9)

Reversing every arrow and reflecting A↔FA\leftrightarrow F, B↔EB\leftrightarrow E, C↔DC\leftrightarrow D produces twenty distinct forbidden orientations (Fig. 2). The other two sites in the eight-site window are ignored, not deleted from the circuit.

Theorem 1 (Canonical FFD classification).

For every open-chain length and every heap DD, the following are equivalent: (i) no translated copy in (8) has a forbidden orientation; (ii) the family (6) satisfies

deg⁡𝖠D\displaystyle\deg\mathsf{A}_{D} ≤sM:=⌈M/3⌉,\displaystyle\leq s_{M}:=\lceil M/3\rceil, (10)
[𝖠D⁢(z),𝖠D⁢(w)]\displaystyle[\mathsf{A}_{D}(z),\mathsf{A}_{D}(w)] =0,\displaystyle=0, (11)
𝖠D⁢(z)⁢𝖠D⁢(−z)\displaystyle\mathsf{A}_{D}(z)\mathsf{A}_{D}(-z) ∈Z⁢(𝒜M)⁢[z2].\displaystyle\in Z(\mathcal{A}_{M})[z^{2}]. (12)

These are identities for arbitrary angles. Sufficiency is proved by exact finite certificates valid at every length.

The criterion takes O⁢(M)O(M) comparisons once the positions of the labels in π\pi are known. All heaps of lengths M≤7M\leq 7 pass. At M=8M=8, precisely 1,0541{,}054 of the 1,4581{,}458 heaps pass; these are counts of heaps, not permutations. A forbidden heap fails the canonical commutation identity generically, although special angle choices can remove the obstruction. Crucially, this does not exclude a different transfer family or an exceptional free spectrum.

Why the criterion works.#

Necessity is genuinely local. Turn off all gates outside a forbidden copy by setting their angles to zero. In its six-generator algebra, the full-support coefficient of [Q1,Q3][Q_{1},Q_{3}], where 𝖠⁢(z)=∑rzr⁢Qr\mathsf{A}(z)=\sum_{r}z^{r}Q_{r}, is nonzero. For the five representatives it is, after division by ∏X=AFyX\prod_{X=A}^{F}y_{X}, respectively

−2⁢xE,−2⁢xF,2⁢xD,2⁢xE,2⁢xF.-2x_{E},\quad-2x_{F},\quad 2x_{D},\quad 2x_{E},\quad 2x_{F}. (13)

Sufficiency has a geometric reduction. The nullity is the number of connected components of FM⁢[S]F_{M}[S] plus the nullity of an auxiliary graph whose vertices are the selected consecutive triangles. Two such triangles are linked according to the temporal order of their middle events. Avoidance forces this auxiliary graph to be a union of paths. A path contributes one to the nullity precisely when it contains an odd number of vertices. Consequently

νD⁢(S)=c⁢(FM⁢[S])+#⁢{odd interlace paths}.\nu_{D}(S)=c(F_{M}[S])+\#\{\text{odd interlace paths}\}. (14)

Only a fixed frontier must be remembered as the chain is scanned; a 32-state transducer evaluates the grade.

Every angle coefficient of the commutator and of the noncentral inversion product then becomes a signed weighted sum recognized by a finite automaton. Exact quotients have 9,7569{,}756 and 7,1957{,}195 states. Their vanishing is certified by invariant subspaces of dimensions 590590 and 427427 over ℚ⁢(z,w)\mathbb{Q}(z,w) and ℚ⁢(z)\mathbb{Q}(z), respectively. The full verification checks all 17,700+12,81017{,}700+12{,}810 transition images. This is an all-length proof, not an extrapolation from short chains. The supplementary material gives the reductions, the finite-state definitions, and executable pseudocode.

From the transfer polynomial to the spectrum.#

Fix a central sector χ\chi. Central inversion becomes

𝖠D,χ⁢(z)⁢𝖠D,χ⁢(−z)=pD,χ⁢(z)⁢𝟏.\mathsf{A}_{D,\chi}(z)\mathsf{A}_{D,\chi}(-z)=p_{D,\chi}(z)\mathbf{1}. (15)

For generic angles, pD,χp_{D,\chi} has sMs_{M} distinct nonzero root pairs {rχ,k,−rχ,k}\{r_{\chi,k},-r_{\chi,k}\}. Simultaneous diagonalization and (15) give

vχ,𝝈=a0∏k=1sM(1+σkrχ,k),𝝈∈𝒞χ.\boxed{v_{\chi,\bm{\sigma}}=a_{0}\prod_{k=1}^{s_{M}}\left(1+\frac{\sigma_{k}}{% r_{\chi,k}}\right),\qquad\bm{\sigma}\in\mathcal{C}_{\chi}.} (16)

The admissible signs form an affine binary code with equal multiplicities. In a fixed irreducible sector they are unrestricted unless M≡1(mod3)M\equiv 1\pmod{3}; in that case one product-of-signs constraint remains. Its value is obtained from the highest transfer coefficient, as explained in Sec. S15.

For real angles on the generic locus, choose rχ,k=i⁢uχ,kr_{\chi,k}=iu_{\chi,k} with uχ,k>0u_{\chi,k}>0. Changing the kkth sign from −1-1 to +1+1 multiplies the eigenvalue by

qχ,k=i⁢uχ,k+1i⁢uχ,k−1=e−i⁢ωχ,k,ωχ,k=2⁢arctan⁡1uχ,k.q_{\chi,k}=\frac{iu_{\chi,k}+1}{iu_{\chi,k}-1}=e^{-i\omega_{\chi,k}},\quad% \omega_{\chi,k}=2\arctan\frac{1}{u_{\chi,k}}. (17)

A fixed-sector parity constraint may require signs to change in pairs. The displayed quantities are the elementary factors, not a claim that every individual flip is allowed in each sector.

Computing the polynomial, not a large matrix.#

The identity coefficient of the inversion product is the positive sum

p0⁢(z)=∑S⁢ feasiblez2⁢νD⁢(S)⁢∏j∈Syj2⁢∏j∉SeD⁢(j,S)=0xj2.p_{0}(z)=\sum_{S\text{ feasible}}z^{2\nu_{D}(S)}\prod_{j\in S}y_{j}^{2}\!\prod% _{\begin{subarray}{c}j\notin S\\ e_{D}(j,S)=0\end{subarray}}x_{j}^{2}. (18)

When inversion is scalar in the full algebra, p0=pD,χp_{0}=p_{D,\chi} for every sector. Centrality alone is not enough to make this replacement. In general one also computes the coefficients supported on ker𝔽2⁡AM\ker_{\mathbb{F}_{2}}A_{M}, where AMA_{M} is the frustration adjacency matrix, and evaluates them in χ\chi. This kernel has dimension at most two. A paired version of the same frontier scan computes all sector polynomials in O⁢(M⁢sM)O(Ms_{M}) arithmetic operations, with a size-independent state bound (Sec. S14). Thus the general root prescription is constructive even when the center is nontrivial.

The familiar half-words I, II, and III are

I\displaystyle\mathrm{I} :(1,2,…,M),\displaystyle:(1,2,\ldots,M), (19)
II\displaystyle\mathrm{II} :(2,4,…,M;1,3,…,M−1),\displaystyle:(2,4,\ldots,M;1,3,\ldots,M-1),
III\displaystyle\mathrm{III} :(3,6,…,M;2,5,…,M−1;1,4,…,M−2),\displaystyle:(3,6,\ldots,M;2,5,\ldots,M-1;1,4,\ldots,M-2),

with the usual even-MM and 3∣M3\mid M conventions in II and III. They pass the local test. These are the regular families solved in Ref. [4]; the present construction also covers heaps without a repeating architecture.

As a nonperiodic example, take M=9M=9, π=(9,4,2,5,7,1,3,8,6)\pi=(9,4,2,5,7,1,3,8,6), and ϕj=0.17+0.029⁢(j−1)+0.004⁢sin⁡j\phi_{j}=0.17+0.029(j-1)+0.004\sin j. Direct evaluation verifies scalar inversion here. The normalized mode polynomial P⁢(x)=p0⁢(i⁢x)/p0⁢(0)P(x)=p_{0}(i\sqrt{x})/p_{0}(0) is

P⁢(x)=\displaystyle P(x)={} 1−1.02263185775715⁢x\displaystyle 1-1.02263185775715x (20)
+0.209346393878477⁢x2\displaystyle+0.209346393878477x^{2}
−0.00725922352756874⁢x3.\displaystyle-0.00725922352756874x^{3}.

The roots are approximately 1.316451.31645, 4.556424.55642, and 22.9658122.96581, with occupation-flip phases 1.4337581.433758, 0.8762250.876225, and 0.4114350.411435. Using unrounded coefficients, the eight eigenvalues from (16), each with multiplicity 6464, agree with an independent 512×512512\times 512 spin-circuit calculation to 1.2×10−141.2\times 10^{-14}.

Scope.#

The result resolves the ordering problem for the canonical nullity-graded transfer construction: acceptance is both necessary and sufficient, and supplies a polynomial-root solution. It does not turn failure of that particular construction into a no-go theorem for every other definition of free-fermion solvability. Repeated roots, vanishing cosines, and other nongeneric points are obtained by limits of the unnormalized polynomial identities; normalized root formulas should not be used there without taking those limits.

Reproducibility.#

The accompanying single-file code archive contains the complete proof sources and certificates, a sector-aware spectral solver, and independent checks. Both formal automata were regenerated byte for byte, all characteristic-zero certificate identities were rerun, and the independent finite audits were repeated. No finite-field specialization is used as the final proof.

Supplementary material#

This supplement contains the complete algebraic reductions, the finite exact certificate argument, and the constructive sector-by-sector spectral solution. The long-chain cancellations use the finite exact certificates included in the archive. The final sections document the independently rerun checks and the accompanying code archive.

S1 Open FFD circuits and heaps#

S1.1 The algebra#

Fix M≥1M\geq 1. The open FFD ∗*-algebra 𝒜M\mathcal{A}_{M} is generated by Hermitian involutions h1,…,hMh_{1},\ldots,h_{M} satisfying

hj2=𝟏,{hj,hk}=0(1≤|j−k|≤2),[hj,hk]=0(|j−k|>2).h_{j}^{2}=\mathbf{1},\qquad\{h_{j},h_{k}\}=0\quad(1\leq|j-k|\leq 2),\qquad[h_{% j},h_{k}]=0\quad(|j-k|>2). (S1)

The frustration graph is

FM=PM2,{j,k}∈E⁢(FM)⟺1≤|j−k|≤2.F_{M}=P_{M}^{2},\qquad\{j,k\}\in E(F_{M})\Longleftrightarrow 1\leq|j-k|\leq 2.

The open chain and its distance-one and distance-two frustration edges are illustrated in figure S1.

Choose a spatial normal order hx=h1x1⁢⋯⁢hMxMh^{x}=h_{1}^{x_{1}}\cdots h_{M}^{x_{M}} for x∈𝔽2Mx\in\mathbb{F}_{2}^{M}. If AMA_{M} is the adjacency matrix of FMF_{M} over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2}, then

hx⁢hy=(−1)x𝖳⁢AM⁢y⁢hy⁢hx.h^{x}h^{y}=(-1)^{x^{\mathsf{T}}A_{M}y}h^{y}h^{x}. (S2)

Hence hxh^{x} is central exactly when AM⁢x=0A_{M}x=0. We write 𝒵M=Z⁢(𝒜M)\mathcal{Z}_{M}=Z(\mathcal{A}_{M}).

S1.2 Palindromic permutation circuits#

For real angles ϕj\phi_{j}, define

uj=exp⁡(i⁢ϕj2⁢hj)=cos⁡(ϕj2)⁢𝟏+i⁢sin⁡(ϕj2)⁢hj.u_{j}=\exp\!\left(\frac{i\phi_{j}}{2}h_{j}\right)=\cos\!\left(\frac{\phi_{j}}{% 2}\right)\mathbf{1}+i\sin\!\left(\frac{\phi_{j}}{2}\right)h_{j}. (S3)

Let TT be the complex-linear anti-involution determined by hjT=hjh_{j}^{T}=h_{j} and (X⁢Y)T=YT⁢XT(XY)^{T}=Y^{T}X^{T}. For a permutation π=(π1,…,πM)\pi=(\pi_{1},\ldots,\pi_{M}), set

Gπ=uπ1⁢⋯⁢uπM,Vπ=Gπ⁢GπT.G_{\pi}=u_{\pi_{1}}\cdots u_{\pi_{M}},\qquad V_{\pi}=G_{\pi}G_{\pi}^{T}. (S4)

Thus the second half retraces the first without complex conjugating the scalar ii. The circuit is a one-pass palindrome: every generator occurs once in the half-word.

S1.3 Heaps: order modulo commuting swaps#

Orient every edge j−kj-k of FMF_{M} from the label that occurs earlier in π\pi to the label that occurs later. The result is an acyclic orientation DπD_{\pi}. Two permutations determine the same orientation exactly when they differ by adjacent exchanges of commuting labels. Since those gates commute, the circuit depends only on the orientation. We call it the heap DD, following the trace-monoid viewpoint [5].

We write v→wv\to w when the edge v⁢wvw is directed from vv to ww. The directed adjacency matrix is

(ED)v⁢w=𝟏{v→w}.(E_{D})_{vw}=\mathbf{1}_{\{v\to w\}}. (S5)

Then ED+ED𝖳=AME_{D}+E_{D}^{\mathsf{T}}=A_{M}.

A convenient insertion encoding will be used by the automata. After the first edge is oriented, a new site jj belongs to the triangle j−2,j−1,jj-2,j-1,j. Transitivity allows exactly three temporal positions: before both old sites, between them, or after both. We denote this ternary choice by qj∈{0,1,2}q_{j}\in\{0,1,2\}. Consequently the number of acyclic orientations is 2⋅3M−22\cdot 3^{M-2} for M≥2M\geq 2.

S2 Exact expansion of the palindrome#

Put

xj=cos⁡ϕj,yj=sin⁡ϕj.x_{j}=\cos\phi_{j},\qquad y_{j}=\sin\phi_{j}. (S6)

The doubled gate is uj2=xj+i⁢yj⁢hju_{j}^{2}=x_{j}+iy_{j}h_{j}. The exact expansion is most transparent if the palindrome is peeled from its outside.

For S⊆[M]S\subseteq[M], define the selected outdegree parity

eD⁢(v,S)=#⁢{w∈S:v→w}(mod2).e_{D}(v,S)=\#\{w\in S:v\to w\}\pmod{2}. (S7)
Definition S1 (Feasible support).

A support S⊆[M]S\subseteq[M] is DD-feasible if

eD⁢(v,S)=0(v∈S).e_{D}(v,S)=0\qquad(v\in S). (S8)

We denote the family by ℱ⁢(D)\mathcal{F}(D).

For S∈ℱ⁢(D)S\in\mathcal{F}(D), let HD⁢(S)H_{D}(S) be the product of the selected generators in any linear extension of D|SD|_{S}. This is well defined because incomparable vertices are nonadjacent in FMF_{M} and hence commute.

Proposition S2 (Exact feasible-support expansion).

The palindrome associated with a heap DD is

VD=∑S∈ℱ⁢(D)aD⁢(S)⁢HD⁢(S),V_{D}=\sum_{S\in\mathcal{F}(D)}a_{D}(S)H_{D}(S), (S9)

where

aD⁢(S)=i|S|⁢∏v∈Syv⁢∏v∉SeD⁢(v,S)=0xv.a_{D}(S)=i^{|S|}\prod_{v\in S}y_{v}\prod_{\begin{subarray}{c}v\notin S\\ e_{D}(v,S)=0\end{subarray}}x_{v}. (S10)
Proof.

Let PP be a graph-Clifford monomial in the generators that lie inside the current pair of gates. Direct multiplication gives

uv⁢P⁢uv={(xv+i⁢yv⁢hv)⁢P,[hv,P]=0,P,{hv,P}=0.u_{v}Pu_{v}=\begin{cases}(x_{v}+iy_{v}h_{v})P,&[h_{v},P]=0,\\ P,&\{h_{v},P\}=0.\end{cases} (S11)

The commutation parity of hvh_{v} with the later selected monomial is exactly eD⁢(v,S)e_{D}(v,S). If it is odd, the two scalar terms and the two hvh_{v}-terms cancel pairwise, leaving PP; hence vv must be absent. If it is even, one may omit vv with factor xvx_{v}, or select it with factor i⁢yviy_{v}. A selected vertex is therefore allowed exactly under (S8). Multiplying the local factors yields (S10). ∎

Remark S3 (Why feasibility is temporal).

The condition is not merely even degree in the induced frustration graph. Only later selected neighbors enter. It therefore depends on the heap orientation. This asymmetry is what permits nonstable feasible supports and is the source of the nontrivial grading below.

S3 The temporal-footprint grading#

The correct spectral degree is not |S||S|. Folded FFD circuits contain composite monomials, including trilinear terms, that carry degree one. The nullity below supplies a grading compatible with the temporal overlap of the selected gates.

S3.1 Temporal adjacency and predecessor footprints#

Let S∈ℱ⁢(D)S\in\mathcal{F}(D), and list its elements in temporal order,

S={s1≺s2≺⋯≺sn}.S=\{s_{1}\prec s_{2}\prec\cdots\prec s_{n}\}.

Define the strictly upper-triangular matrix N=ND,S∈Mn⁢(𝔽2)N=N_{D,S}\in M_{n}(\mathbb{F}_{2}) by

Na⁢b=𝟏{a<b, 1≤|sa−sb|≤2}.N_{ab}=\mathbf{1}_{\{a<b,\;1\leq|s_{a}-s_{b}|\leq 2\}}. (S12)

Thus row aa records the later selected generators that anticommute with hsah_{s_{a}}, and feasibility is

N⁢𝟏=0.N\mathbf{1}=0. (S13)

For the later event sas_{a}, define its closed predecessor footprint

pa=𝐞a+∑c<aNc⁢a⁢𝐞c.p_{a}=\mathbf{e}_{a}+\sum_{c<a}N_{ca}\mathbf{e}_{c}. (S14)

The footprint marks the event itself and every earlier selected event whose commutation parity is flipped by selecting sas_{a}. If the footprints are placed as columns, then

B=(p1⁢⋯⁢pn)=I+N.B=(p_{1}\ \cdots\ p_{n})=I+N. (S15)

Their binary Gram matrix is

G=B𝖳⁢B=I+N+N𝖳+N𝖳⁢N.G=B^{\mathsf{T}}B=I+N+N^{\mathsf{T}}+N^{\mathsf{T}}N. (S16)

The diagonal of GG is unavoidable self-overlap. Since BB is unitriangular, GG is always nonsingular and its full nullity is trivial. The mutual overlaps are captured by deleting the diagonal.

Definition S4 (Canonical grading matrix).

Set

KD⁢(S)=offdiag⁡[(I+ND,S)𝖳⁢(I+ND,S)]=N+N𝖳+offdiag⁡(N𝖳⁢N),K_{D}(S)=\operatorname{offdiag}\!\left[(I+N_{D,S})^{\mathsf{T}}(I+N_{D,S})% \right]=N+N^{\mathsf{T}}+\operatorname{offdiag}(N^{\mathsf{T}}N), (S17)

and define

νD⁢(S)=nullity𝔽2⁡KD⁢(S).\nu_{D}(S)=\operatorname{nullity}_{\mathbb{F}_{2}}K_{D}(S). (S18)

For a≠ba\neq b, the entry has the explicit form

(KD⁢(S))a⁢b=𝟏{sa∼sb}+#⁢{c:sc≺sa,sb,sc∼sa,sb}(mod2).(K_{D}(S))_{ab}=\mathbf{1}_{\{s_{a}\sim s_{b}\}}+\#\{c:s_{c}\prec s_{a},s_{b},% \ s_{c}\sim s_{a},s_{b}\}\pmod{2}. (S19)

The first term is direct anticommutation. The second counts common temporal predecessors: two later selected events overlap when they flip the same earlier parity register.

Example S5 (One temporal fork).

For

N=(011000000),N=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&1\\ 0&0&0\\ 0&0&0\end{pmatrix},

the direct frustration graph is a two-leaf star. The common predecessor adds the leaf-to-leaf edge, and

K=(011101110)K=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&1\\ 1&0&1\\ 1&1&0\end{pmatrix}

has binary nullity one. Thus this feasible trilinear monomial has spectral degree one.

S3.2 Elementary properties#

Lemma S6 (Basic grading properties).

For every feasible support SS:

  1. (a)

    νD⁢(S)\nu_{D}(S) is independent of the chosen linear extension;

  2. (b)

  4. (d)

Adjacent exchanges between linear extensions involve incomparable, hence nonadjacent, vertices. They only permute matching rows and columns of KD⁢(S)K_{D}(S), proving (a).

For (b), feasibility gives N⁢𝟏=0N\mathbf{1}=0. Over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2},

diag⁡(N𝖳⁢N)=N𝖳⁢𝟏,offdiag⁡(N𝖳⁢N)⁢𝟏=N𝖳⁢𝟏.\operatorname{diag}(N^{\mathsf{T}}N)=N^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{1},\qquad% \operatorname{offdiag}(N^{\mathsf{T}}N)\mathbf{1}=N^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{1}.

KD⁢(S)⁢𝟏=N⁢𝟏+N𝖳⁢𝟏+N𝖳⁢𝟏=0.K_{D}(S)\mathbf{1}=N\mathbf{1}+N^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{1}+N^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{% 1}=0.

Reversing HD⁢(S)H_{D}(S) introduces one minus sign for every edge of FM⁢[S]F_{M}[S]. The number of such edges is the sum of the selected outdegrees in D⁢[S]D[S], which is even by feasibility. Hence the monomial is Hermitian, proving (d). ∎

The identity KD⁢(S)⁢𝟏=0K_{D}(S)\mathbf{1}=0 is also a useful retrospective explanation for the correction N𝖳⁢NN^{\mathsf{T}}N. The direct frustration matrix N+N𝖳N+N^{\mathsf{T}} need not be singular on a feasible support. The common-predecessor term cancels its residual column-parity vector exactly.

S4 Forbidden heaps and the Baxter property#

S4.1 The six-vertex obstruction#

Let HH have vertices A,B,C,D,E,FA,B,C,D,E,F and edges

E⁢(H)={A⁢B,B⁢C,B⁢D,C⁢D,C⁢E,D⁢E,E⁢F}.E(H)=\{AB,BC,BD,CD,CE,DE,EF\}. (S23)

It consists of two triangles B⁢C⁢DBCD and C⁢D⁢ECDE sharing the edge C⁢DCD, with pendant edges A⁢BAB and E⁢FEF.

For a word containing the six letters once, orient every edge from the earlier letter to the later one. Let τ\tau reverse the word, and let ρ\rho be the spatial reflection

A↔F,B↔E,C↔D.A\leftrightarrow F,\qquad B\leftrightarrow E,\qquad C\leftrightarrow D.

Start from the five temporal orders

A⁢D⁢B⁢C⁢F⁢E,A⁢D⁢B⁢C⁢E⁢F,A⁢C⁢B⁢F⁢E⁢D,A⁢C⁢B⁢D⁢F⁢E,A⁢C⁢B⁢D⁢E⁢F,ADBCFE,\qquad ADBCEF,\qquad ACBFED,\qquad ACBDFE,\qquad ACBDEF, (S24)

where spaces are inserted only for readability. Applying τϵ⁢ρδ\tau^{\epsilon}\rho^{\delta}, ϵ,δ∈{0,1}\epsilon,\delta\in\{0,1\}, gives twenty distinct orientations. Their set is denoted 𝔅\mathfrak{B}. A complete seven-bit signature list is given in section S16.

For 1≤a≤M−71\leq a\leq M-7, the sites

A=a,B=a+2,C=a+3,D=a+4,E=a+5,F=a+7A=a,\quad B=a+2,\quad C=a+3,\quad D=a+4,\quad E=a+5,\quad F=a+7 (S25)

induce a copy Ha⊂PM2H_{a}\subset P_{M}^{2}.

Definition S9 (HH-avoidance).

A heap DD is HH-avoiding if D|Ha∉𝔅D|_{H_{a}}\notin\mathfrak{B} for every allowed translation aa.

S4.2 Canonical Baxter property#

Let

sM=α⁢(PM2)=⌈M3⌉.s_{M}=\alpha(P_{M}^{2})=\left\lceil\frac{M}{3}\right\rceil. (S26)

All angle identities are understood in the quotient ring

ℛM=ℂ[x1,y1,…,xM,yM]/(xj2+yj2−1:1≤j≤M).\mathscr{R}_{M}=\mathbb{C}[x_{1},y_{1},\ldots,x_{M},y_{M}]/(x_{j}^{2}+y_{j}^{2% }-1:1\leq j\leq M). (S27)
Definition S10 (Canonical Baxter property).

A heap DD has the canonical Baxter property if

degz⁡𝖠D⁢(z)\displaystyle\deg_{z}\mathsf{A}_{D}(z) ≤sM,\displaystyle\leq s_{M}, (S28)
[𝖠D⁢(z),𝖠D⁢(w)]\displaystyle[\mathsf{A}_{D}(z),\mathsf{A}_{D}(w)] =0,\displaystyle=0, (S29)
𝖠D⁢(z)⁢𝖠D⁢(−z)\displaystyle\mathsf{A}_{D}(z)\mathsf{A}_{D}(-z) ∈𝒵M⁢[z2].\displaystyle\in\mathcal{Z}_{M}[z^{2}]. (S30)

Theorem 1 says that this property is equivalent to avoiding the twenty local orientations.

S5 Physical consequence: a product spectrum#

The algebraic theorem immediately implies the usual free-fermion spectral form. We include the derivation because it explains why the three Baxter conditions are the right target.

An affine sign code 𝒞⊆{±1}s\mathcal{C}\subseteq\{\pm 1\}^{s} is a coset of a subgroup under componentwise multiplication; equivalently, it is defined by parity equations

∏k=1sσkcℓ⁢k=ζℓ,cℓ⁢k∈𝔽2,ζℓ∈{±1}.\prod_{k=1}^{s}\sigma_{k}^{c_{\ell k}}=\zeta_{\ell},\qquad c_{\ell k}\in% \mathbb{F}_{2},\quad\zeta_{\ell}\in\{\pm 1\}.
Theorem S11 (Baxter identities and the FFD spectrum).

Suppose DD has the canonical Baxter property. On a Zariski-open set of angle parameters, the following holds in every irreducible central sector χ\chi. The charges have a common, zz-independent eigenspace decomposition, and their joint eigenvalue polynomials are

Λχ,𝝈⁢(z)=a0⁢∏k=1sM(1+σk⁢λχ,k⁢z),𝝈∈𝒞χ,\Lambda_{\chi,\bm{\sigma}}(z)=a_{0}\prod_{k=1}^{s_{M}}(1+\sigma_{k}\lambda_{% \chi,k}z),\qquad\bm{\sigma}\in\mathcal{C}_{\chi}, (S31)

where the nonzero λχ,k\lambda_{\chi,k} are distinct up to sign, 𝒞χ\mathcal{C}_{\chi} is an affine sign code, and every allowed sign vector occurs with the same multiplicity. Conversely, a common eigenbasis with the product form (S31) implies the canonical Baxter property.

Proof.

By corollary S8, the operators i−r⁢QD,ri^{-r}Q_{D,r} are Hermitian. Commutation therefore gives a common eigenbasis in each central sector. Let Λa⁢(z)\Lambda_{a}(z) be one joint eigenvalue polynomial. The degree and constant term obey

deg⁡Λa≤sM,Λa⁢(0)=a0.\deg\Lambda_{a}\leq s_{M},\qquad\Lambda_{a}(0)=a_{0}.

Central inversion becomes a scalar identity

Λa⁢(z)⁢Λa⁢(−z)=Pχ⁢(z2),\Lambda_{a}(z)\Lambda_{a}(-z)=P_{\chi}(z^{2}), (S32)

with the same polynomial PχP_{\chi} for every joint eigenspace in the sector.

To see the generic root structure, specialize all angles outside the maximal stable set

I={1,4,7,…}∩[M],|I|=sM,I=\{1,4,7,\ldots\}\cap[M],\qquad|I|=s_{M},

to yj=0,xj=1y_{j}=0,x_{j}=1. Every surviving support lies in II, so N=K=0N=K=0 and νD⁢(S)=|S|\nu_{D}(S)=|S|. Hence, independently of the heap,

𝖠D⁢(z)=∏j∈I(xj+i⁢z⁢yj⁢hj),\mathsf{A}_{D}(z)=\prod_{j\in I}(x_{j}+izy_{j}h_{j}), (S33)

and

Pχ⁢(z2)=∏j∈I(xj2+yj2⁢z2).P_{\chi}(z^{2})=\prod_{j\in I}(x_{j}^{2}+y_{j}^{2}z^{2}).

At generic values this polynomial has sMs_{M} distinct nonzero root pairs. Therefore, away from a proper algebraic subset,

Pχ⁢(z2)=a02⁢∏k=1sM(1−λχ,k2⁢z2).P_{\chi}(z^{2})=a_{0}^{2}\prod_{k=1}^{s_{M}}(1-\lambda_{\chi,k}^{2}z^{2}). (S34)

A polynomial Λa\Lambda_{a} satisfying (S32) contains exactly one zero from every pair {λχ,k−1,−λχ,k−1}\{\lambda_{\chi,k}^{-1},-\lambda_{\chi,k}^{-1}\}. It cannot contain both, because that would make a double zero in the product, and it cannot contain neither. This proves (S31) with some sign vector.

At the decoupled point, the commuting generators hjh_{j}, j∈Ij\in I, span an isotropic subspace of the graph-Clifford commutation form. In a fixed central sector, their simultaneous characters are exactly those whose restriction to the central intersection agrees with χ\chi; this is an affine sign code. Any two admissible characters are related by conjugation with a graph-Clifford monomial, so their multiplicities agree. Analytic continuation on the generic locus can only permute root pairs and exchange the two roots inside a pair, which acts by a signed permutation and preserves the affine-code property.

Conversely, a common product eigenbasis makes all charges commute. The product with z↦−zz\mapsto-z is scalar in every irreducible representation, hence central in the finite-dimensional semisimple algebra. The degree bound is immediate. ∎

The constructive sector polynomials, the exact sign constraints, and the reality of the generic physical root pairs are developed in Secs. S14 and S15. In particular, central inversion must not be silently replaced by scalar inversion in the full algebra.

S6 Necessity: the local forbidden obstruction#

The reverse implication in theorem 1 is local and exact.

Theorem S12 (Six-site obstruction).

Among the seventy-two acyclic orientations of HH, the twenty orientations in 𝔅\mathfrak{B} are exactly those for which the coefficient of the full-support monomial hA⁢hB⁢hC⁢hD⁢hE⁢hFh_{A}h_{B}h_{C}h_{D}h_{E}h_{F} in [QD,1,QD,3][Q_{D,1},Q_{D,3}] is nonzero. For the five representatives (S24), after factoring ∏X=AFyX\prod_{X=A}^{F}y_{X}, the coefficients are

−2⁢xE,−2⁢xF,2⁢xD,2⁢xE,2⁢xF.-2x_{E},\qquad-2x_{F},\qquad 2x_{D},\qquad 2x_{E},\qquad 2x_{F}. (S35)
Proof.

There are only seventy-two orientations and sixty-four supports. The supplied exact verifier enumerates the feasible supports, constructs KD⁢(S)K_{D}(S) by binary arithmetic, retains the degree-one and degree-three terms, and multiplies graph-Clifford monomials in a fixed spatial normal order. It finds nonzero full-support coefficients in exactly the twenty stated orientations.

The calculation can be inspected by hand in each representative. For the temporal order A⁢C⁢B⁢D⁢E⁢FACBDEF, for instance,

Q1⊃i⁢xF⁢yB⁢yC⁢yE⁢hB⁢hC⁢hE,Q3⊃−i⁢yA⁢yD⁢yF⁢hA⁢hD⁢hF.Q_{1}\supset ix_{F}y_{B}y_{C}y_{E}\,h_{B}h_{C}h_{E},\qquad Q_{3}\supset-iy_{A}% y_{D}y_{F}\,h_{A}h_{D}h_{F}.

The supports are complementary and the monomials anticommute. Their commutator contributes

2⁢xF⁢∏X=AFyX⁢hA⁢hB⁢hC⁢hD⁢hE⁢hF,2x_{F}\prod_{X=A}^{F}y_{X}\,h_{A}h_{B}h_{C}h_{D}h_{E}h_{F},

and there is no second pair with the same full support. The remaining representatives are equally short. Temporal reversal and spatial reflection give the other fifteen forbidden orientations. ∎

Corollary S13 (Forbidden copy implies failure).

If a heap DD contains a translated copy HaH_{a} with orientation in 𝔅\mathfrak{B}, then DD does not have the canonical Baxter property.

Proof.

Specialize all angles outside the six sites to xj=1,yj=0x_{j}=1,y_{j}=0. The corresponding gates become the identity, and the six-site coefficient from theorem S12 survives. Hence [QD,1,QD,3][Q_{D,1},Q_{D,3}] is not the zero polynomial. ∎

The degree estimate does not require HH-avoidance.

Theorem S14 (Sink-nullity bound).

For every heap DD and every feasible support SS,

νD⁢(S)≤|Sink⁡(D⁢[S])|.\nu_{D}(S)\leq|\operatorname{Sink}(D[S])|. (S36)

Consequently

degz⁡𝖠D⁢(z)≤⌈M3⌉\deg_{z}\mathsf{A}_{D}(z)\leq\left\lceil\frac{M}{3}\right\rceil (S37)

for every heap.

The proof establishes injectivity of the restriction map

Suppose q∈ker⁡KD⁢(S)q\in\ker K_{D}(S) and qv=0q_{v}=0 at every sink. We must prove q=0q=0. By (S19), the matrix has spatial bandwidth four: (KD⁢(S))i⁢j=0(K_{D}(S))_{ij}=0 whenever |i−j|>4|i-j|>4. This permits a left-to-right scan that retains only four sites.

S7.1 Local scan#

A boundary state records, for each retained site,

(real,selected,qv,current residual of ⁢(K⁢q)v),(\text{real},\text{selected},q_{v},\text{current residual of }(Kq)_{v}),

together with the orientations of distance-one and distance-two edges in the window. On appending a new site tt:

  1. 1.

    insert the direct PM2P_{M}^{2} contributions between tt and t−1,t−2t-1,t-2;

  2. 2.

    finalize the selected out-neighborhood of k=t−2k=t-2, whose possible neighbors all lie in {k−2,k−1,k+1,k+2}\{k-2,k-1,k+1,k+2\};

  3. 3.

    enforce feasibility at kk;

    if kk has no selected out-neighbor, enforce the sink condition qk=0q_{k}=0;

Acyclicity is local because PM2P_{M}^{2} is chordal: it is enough to require every consecutive triangle to be transitively oriented.

S7.2 Finite closure certificate#

The exact state counts after one, two, three, and four real sites are

3,18,96,504.3,\qquad 18,\qquad 96,\qquad 504.

Closing the transition relation under arbitrary additional sites stabilizes at

908908 (S39)

reachable states. Exactly 191191 of them can be flushed through the right boundary. None of these flushable states has ever encountered qv=1q_{v}=1. Therefore a kernel vector vanishing on all sinks is zero, proving (S36).

Finally, two adjacent selected vertices cannot both be sinks. Thus the sinks form a stable set of PM2P_{M}^{2}, and

|Sink⁡(D⁢[S])|≤α⁢(PM2)=⌈M3⌉.|\operatorname{Sink}(D[S])|\leq\alpha(P_{M}^{2})=\left\lceil\frac{M}{3}\right\rceil.

This proves (S37).

Remark S15 (Nature of the certificate).

The state set is not a bounded-size check in MM; it is a closed transition system. Once closure is reached, every longer scan remains inside the same finite set. The certificate therefore proves the inequality at every length.

S8 A triangle-interlace formula for the grading#

The grading matrix KD⁢(S)K_{D}(S) is defined in temporal coordinates. For the finite-state proof it is useful to replace it by a spatially banded matrix on consecutive triangles.

Let S∈ℱ⁢(D)S\in\mathcal{F}(D) and put

GS=PM2⁢[S].G_{S}=P_{M}^{2}[S].

For every ii such that i,i+1,i+2∈Si,i+1,i+2\in S, let τi\tau_{i} be the three-edge cycle on these vertices. Write

T⁢(S)={i:i,i+1,i+2∈S}.T(S)=\{i:i,i+1,i+2\in S\}. (S40)

The oriented triangle is transitive. Its temporal median mi∈{i,i+1,i+2}m_{i}\in\{i,i+1,i+2\} is the unique vertex with one incoming and one outgoing triangle edge.

Define the alternating matrix ΩD⁢[T⁢(S)]\Omega_{D}[T(S)], indexed by T⁢(S)T(S), by

Ωi,i+1\displaystyle\Omega_{i,i+1} =1+𝟏{mi=mi+1},\displaystyle=1+\mathbf{1}_{\{m_{i}=m_{i+1}\}}, (S41)
Ωi,i+2\displaystyle\Omega_{i,i+2} =𝟏{mi=mi+2},\displaystyle=\mathbf{1}_{\{m_{i}=m_{i+2}\}}, (S42)

and Ωi⁢j=0\Omega_{ij}=0 for |i−j|>2|i-j|>2.

Theorem S16 (Triangle-interlace formula).

For every heap DD and every feasible support SS,

νD(S)=c(GS)+nullity𝔽2ΩD[T(S)],\boxed{\displaystyle\nu_{D}(S)=c(G_{S})+\operatorname{nullity}_{\mathbb{F}_{2}% }\Omega_{D}[T(S)],} (S43)

where c⁢(GS)c(G_{S}) is the number of connected components, with c⁢(∅)=0c(\varnothing)=0.

Proof.

Let BB be the unoriented vertex-edge incidence matrix of GSG_{S} over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2}. Let PP be the tail-incidence matrix,

Pv,e=1⟺v⁢ is the tail of the oriented edge ⁢e.P_{v,e}=1\Longleftrightarrow v\text{ is the tail of the oriented edge }e.

Feasibility makes the diagonal vanish in the identity

ND,S=P⁢B𝖳.N_{D,S}=PB^{\mathsf{T}}. (S44)

Indeed, off the diagonal the right-hand side records the orientation, while its diagonal records selected outdegree parity.

The grading matrix can be written

KD⁢(S)=B⁢B𝖳+ND,S𝖳⁢ND,S.K_{D}(S)=BB^{\mathsf{T}}+N_{D,S}^{\mathsf{T}}N_{D,S}. (S45)

Off the diagonal this is the direct adjacency plus common-predecessor parity. On the diagonal, B⁢B𝖳BB^{\mathsf{T}} contributes degree parity and N𝖳⁢NN^{\mathsf{T}}N contributes indegree parity; their sum is outdegree parity, which vanishes. Substituting (S44) gives

KD⁢(S)=B⁢J⁢B𝖳,J=I+P𝖳⁢P.K_{D}(S)=BJB^{\mathsf{T}},\qquad J=I+P^{\mathsf{T}}P. (S46)

For a fixed tail, the outgoing edges form one block of JJ, and that block is the adjacency matrix of a complete graph on an even number of vertices. Over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2}, the adjacency matrix of an even complete graph squares to the identity. Hence

J2=I.J^{2}=I. (S47)

Let Z=ker⁡BZ=\ker B be the cycle space of GSG_{S}. Since im⁡B𝖳=Z⟂\operatorname{im}B^{\mathsf{T}}=Z^{\perp}, multiplication by B𝖳B^{\mathsf{T}} gives an exact sequence

0⟶ker⁡B𝖳⟶ker⁡(B⁢J⁢B𝖳)⟶Z⟂∩J⁢Z⟶0.0\longrightarrow\ker B^{\mathsf{T}}\longrightarrow\ker(BJB^{\mathsf{T}})% \longrightarrow Z^{\perp}\cap JZ\longrightarrow 0. (S48)

The first term has dimension c⁢(GS)c(G_{S}). Because JJ is involutory, multiplication by JJ identifies the intersection with the radical of the bilinear form

β⁢(z,z′)=z𝖳⁢J⁢z′\beta(z,z^{\prime})=z^{\mathsf{T}}Jz^{\prime} (S49)

restricted to ZZ. Therefore

νD⁢(S)=c⁢(GS)+dimrad⁡(β|Z).\nu_{D}(S)=c(G_{S})+\dim\operatorname{rad}(\beta|_{Z}). (S50)

Every induced subgraph of PM2P_{M}^{2} is chordal and has clique number at most three. Its cycle space is generated by consecutive triangles. These cycles are independent because the distance-two edge {i,i+2}\{i,i+2\} occurs only in τi\tau_{i}. Thus {τi:i∈T⁢(S)}\{\tau_{i}:i\in T(S)\} is a basis of ZZ.

In this basis,

β⁢(τi,τj)=τi𝖳⁢τj+(P⁢τi)𝖳⁢(P⁢τj).\beta(\tau_{i},\tau_{j})=\tau_{i}^{\mathsf{T}}\tau_{j}+(P\tau_{i})^{\mathsf{T}% }(P\tau_{j}).

Inside a transitively oriented triangle, the parity of outgoing triangle edges equals one only at the temporal median. Hence

P⁢τi=𝐞mi.P\tau_{i}=\mathbf{e}_{m_{i}}. (S51)

Consecutive triangles share one edge, triangles two positions apart share no edge but may have the same median, and more distant triangles have neither contribution. Equations (S41)–(S42) are exactly the matrix entries of β|Z\beta|_{Z}. Taking its radical dimension in (S50) proves the theorem. ∎

S9 Why the forbidden patterns make the grading finite-state#

We now show that HH-avoidance turns the triangle-interlace graph into a path forest. This is the key structural reason the grading can be recognized by a small automaton.

Use zero-based sites temporarily and write

ci=𝟏{i→i+1},di=𝟏{i→i+2}.c_{i}=\mathbf{1}_{\{i\to i+1\}},\qquad d_{i}=\mathbf{1}_{\{i\to i+2\}}. (S52)

Transitivity of each consecutive triangle is

ci=ci+1⟹di=ci.c_{i}=c_{i+1}\Longrightarrow d_{i}=c_{i}. (S53)

The interlace graph has vertex set T⁢(S)T(S) and edges

i∼i+1\displaystyle i\sim i+1 ⟺mi≠mi+1,\displaystyle\Longleftrightarrow m_{i}\neq m_{i+1}, (S54)
i∼i+2\displaystyle i\sim i+2 ⟺mi=mi+2.\displaystyle\Longleftrightarrow m_{i}=m_{i+2}. (S55)

There are no longer-range edges.

Lemma S17 (A non-path contains a local triangle).

If ΩD⁢[T⁢(S)]\Omega_{D}[T(S)] is not a disjoint union of paths, then three consecutive triangle indices i,i+1,i+2i,i+1,i+2 span a triangle.

Proof.

If i∼i+2i\sim i+2, the allowed ranges of the medians force

mi=mi+2=i+2.m_{i}=m_{i+2}=i+2.

Then

i∼i+1⟺mi+1≠i+2⟺i+1∼i+2.i\sim i+1\Longleftrightarrow m_{i+1}\neq i+2\Longleftrightarrow i+1\sim i+2.

Thus a distance-two edge has either both adjacent edges or neither. In the absence of a local triangle, every vertex has degree at most two. A cycle is also impossible: its leftmost vertex would have neighbors i+1i+1 and i+2i+2, and the displayed equivalence would complete a triangle. Hence every component is a path. ∎

A local interlace triangle uses five consecutive selected sites. Enumerating the transitive orientations of the three overlapping spatial triangles gives four seeds:

c0⁢c1⁢c2⁢c3d0⁢d1⁢d2(m0,m1,m2)0101001(2,1,2)0101011(2,3,2)1010100(2,3,2)1010110(2,1,2).\begin{array}[]{c|c|c}c_{0}c_{1}c_{2}c_{3}&d_{0}d_{1}d_{2}&(m_{0},m_{1},m_{2})% \\ \hline\cr 0101&001&(2,1,2)\\ 0101&011&(2,3,2)\\ 1010&100&(2,3,2)\\ 1010&110&(2,1,2).\end{array} (S56)

Let sj=𝟏{j∈S}s_{j}=\mathbf{1}_{\{j\in S\}}. Feasibility at a selected site jj is

sj−2⁢(1+dj−2)+sj−1⁢(1+cj−1)+sj+1⁢cj+sj+2⁢dj=0.s_{j-2}(1+d_{j-2})+s_{j-1}(1+c_{j-1})+s_{j+1}c_{j}+s_{j+2}d_{j}=0. (S57)

The remaining propagation is finite. For the seed (1010;100)(1010;100), transitivity forces c4=d4=1c_{4}=d_{4}=1, and the translated H0H_{0} has signature 110011⁢d5110011d_{5}, one of two forbidden signatures. For the seed (0101;001)(0101;001), runs of lengths R=5,6,7R=5,6,7 immediately produce a forbidden signature. Longer runs enter one of three states Pn,Qn,RnP_{n},Q_{n},R_{n}. statecn+1outcomePn01110011⁢ forbiddenPn1violates transitivityQn01111101⁢ forbiddenQn1Pn+1Rn0Qn+1Rn1Rn+1.\begin{array}[]{c|c|l}\text{state}&c_{n+1}&\text{outcome}\\ \hline\cr P_{n}&0&1110011\text{ forbidden}\\ P_{n}&1&\text{violates transitivity}\\ Q_{n}&0&1111101\text{ forbidden}\\ Q_{n}&1&P_{n+1}\\ R_{n}&0&Q_{n+1}\\ R_{n}&1&R_{n+1}.\end{array} (S61)

Theorem S18 (Forbidden-HH path dichotomy).

Let DD be an acyclic orientation of PM2P_{M}^{2} and SS a feasible support. If ΩD⁢[T⁢(S)]\Omega_{D}[T(S)] is not a disjoint union of paths, then DD contains one of the twenty forbidden orientations. In particular, for an HH-avoiding heap,

ΩD⁢[T⁢(S)]⁢ is a path forest for every feasible ⁢S.\Omega_{D}[T(S)]\text{ is a path forest for every feasible }S. (S62)
Proof.

By lemma S17, a non-path graph contains a local interlace triangle. Its orientation is one of the four seeds (S56). The preceding propagation forces a forbidden HH for the two right-propagating seeds, and spatial reflection handles the other two. ∎

The binary adjacency matrix of a path on qq vertices has nullity one for odd qq and zero for even qq. Combining theorems S16 and S18 gives the finite-state grading formula.

Corollary S19 (Path grading).

If DD is HH-avoiding and SS is feasible, then

νD(S)=c(PM2[S])+oD(S),\boxed{\displaystyle\nu_{D}(S)=c(P_{M}^{2}[S])+o_{D}(S),} (S63)

where oD⁢(S)o_{D}(S) is the number of odd-order connected components of the triangle-interlace path forest.

The first term starts a new component exactly when a selected site is preceded by two unselected sites. The second term can be accumulated by retaining only the last two triangle vertices, their connectivity, and the parity of every interlace component that still meets this boundary. After exact minimization, the combined grading transducer has thirty-two reachable states.

S10 Coefficientwise reduction of the Baxter identities#

We now reduce the operator identities to two families of signed scalar sums. This step is exact and uses no automata.

S10.1 Local quotient basis#

Consider a product of two coefficients aD⁢(X)⁢aD⁢(Y)a_{D}(X)a_{D}(Y). At any site, the degree in xv,yvx_{v},y_{v} is at most two. Modulo xv2+yv2=1x_{v}^{2}+y_{v}^{2}=1, the degree-two subspace has the basis

ℳ={1,xv,yv,xv2,xv⁢yv}.\mathcal{M}=\{1,x_{v},y_{v},x_{v}^{2},x_{v}y_{v}\}. (S64)

Indeed, yv2=1−xv2y_{v}^{2}=1-x_{v}^{2}, and the five displayed functions are independent. Therefore it is enough to prove vanishing separately for every full basis word

𝒎=∏v=1Mmv,mv∈ℳ.\bm{m}=\prod_{v=1}^{M}m_{v},\qquad m_{v}\in\mathcal{M}. (S65)

Fix the output graph-Clifford support R∈𝔽2MR\in\mathbb{F}_{2}^{M}. Write the two supports as

Y=X△R=X+RY=X\mathbin{\triangle}R=X+R (S66)

over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2}. Let

p=ED⁢X,r=ED⁢R.p=E_{D}X,\qquad r=E_{D}R. (S67)

Then the selected outdegree parities of XX and YY are pp and p+rp+r, respectively.

At a site vv, compatibility of the pair with feasibility and the chosen basis symbol is exactly one of the five rows in table S1. We call the rows of the first and fourth form type A\mathrm{A}, the second and fifth type B\mathrm{B}, and the third type C\mathrm{C}.

Lemma S20 (Local compatibility).

The rows of table S1 are necessary and sufficient. All other combinations of (Rv,rv,mv)(R_{v},r_{v},m_{v}) contribute zero.

Proof.

If Rv=1R_{v}=1, exactly one of Xv,YvX_{v},Y_{v} is selected. When rv=0r_{v}=0, both supports see the same outdegree parity, which must be zero for the selected support; the unselected support contributes xvx_{v}, giving xv⁢yvx_{v}y_{v}. When rv=1r_{v}=1, feasibility forces the unselected support to have odd parity, so it contributes no xvx_{v}; the local symbol is yvy_{v}. The condition distinguishing which support is selected is pv+Xv=1p_{v}+X_{v}=1.

If Rv=0R_{v}=0, the two supports agree at vv. When rv=1r_{v}=1, simultaneous selection is impossible, and the two absent copies have opposite parity, so exactly one contributes xvx_{v}. When rv=0r_{v}=0, both absent copies give xv2x_{v}^{2}, while simultaneous selection gives yv2=1−xv2y_{v}^{2}=1-x_{v}^{2}; this creates the two final rows. The displayed equations are precisely the feasibility conditions in each case. ∎

Because pvp_{v} depends only on XX in the spatial window v−2,…,v+2v-2,\ldots,v+2, these constraints have radius two. For fixed (D,R,𝒎)(D,R,\bm{m}), their solution set is an affine binary space, denoted

𝒳⁢(D,R,𝒎)⊆𝔽2M.\mathcal{X}(D,R,\bm{m})\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{2}^{M}. (S68)

Let X,Y=X+RX,Y=X+R be feasible. Then

S10.3 The two sign characters#

Let 𝒯A,𝒯B,𝒯C\mathcal{T}_{A},\mathcal{T}_{B},\mathcal{T}_{C} be the sets of sites of the three local types. If Δ\Delta is a homogeneous direction of the affine fibre, the table gives

(ED⁢Δ)v=0(v∈𝒯A),(ED⁢Δ)v=Δv(v∈𝒯B),Δv=0(v∈𝒯C).(E_{D}\Delta)_{v}=0\quad(v\in\mathcal{T}_{A}),\qquad(E_{D}\Delta)_{v}=\Delta_{% v}\quad(v\in\mathcal{T}_{B}),\qquad\Delta_{v}=0\quad(v\in\mathcal{T}_{C}). (S71)

Lemma S22 (Fibre sign characters).

On every nonempty fibre, after factoring a nonzero scalar independent of XX, the commutator and inversion signs are respectively

ϵC⁢(X)\displaystyle\epsilon_{\mathrm{C}}(X) =(−1)|𝒯B∩X|,\displaystyle=(-1)^{|\mathcal{T}_{B}\cap X|}, (S72)

The inversion summand contains the additional factor (−1)νD⁢(Y)(-1)^{\nu_{D}(Y)}. By lemma S6, translating by Δ\Delta changes this factor by (−1)|Δ|(-1)^{|\Delta|}. S10.4 The scalar coefficient sums#

Proposition S23 (Coefficient reduction).

To prove the forward implication in theorem 1, it is enough to prove the following two identities for every HH-avoiding heap DD, every RR, and every basis word 𝐦\bm{m}:

CD,R,𝒎⁢(z,w)\displaystyle C_{D,R,\bm{m}}(z,w) =∑X∈𝒳⁢(D,R,𝒎)(−1)|𝒯B∩X|⁢zνD⁢(X)⁢wνD⁢(X+R)=0\displaystyle=\sum_{X\in\mathcal{X}(D,R,\bm{m})}(-1)^{|\mathcal{T}_{B}\cap X|}% z^{\nu_{D}(X)}w^{\nu_{D}(X+R)}=0 if ⁢e⁢(R)=1,\displaystyle\text{if }e(R)=1, (S74)
ID,R,𝒎⁢(z)\displaystyle I_{D,R,\bm{m}}(z) =∑X∈𝒳⁢(D,R,𝒎)(−1)|𝒯A∩X|⁢zνD⁢(X)+νD⁢(X+R)=0\displaystyle=\sum_{X\in\mathcal{X}(D,R,\bm{m})}(-1)^{|\mathcal{T}_{A}\cap X|}% z^{\nu_{D}(X)+\nu_{D}(X+R)}=0 if ⁢AM⁢R≠0.\displaystyle\text{if }A_{M}R\neq 0. (S75)
Proof.

Fix RR and 𝒎\bm{m}. By lemma S20, the contributing support pairs are exactly the fibre. If e⁢(R)=0e(R)=0, the two graph-Clifford monomials commute and the commutator contribution vanishes before summation. If e⁢(R)=1e(R)=1, their difference is twice one order, and lemma S22 gives (S74) up to a fixed nonzero scalar. Similarly, (S70) isolates the noncentral inversion coefficients, and the inversion part of lemma S22 gives (S75). S11 Finite weighted automata for all coefficients#

The sums (S74)–(S75) are finite-state because every ingredient has bounded spatial memory:

  • •

    acyclic orientations are generated by the ternary insertion symbol qq;

  • •

    HH-avoidance is a regular language of fixed forbidden windows;

  • •

    the compatibility table has radius two;

  • •

    the path grading (S63) is recognized by a finite transducer;

  • •

    the two signs, e⁢(R)e(R), and noncentrality are parity accumulators.

S11.1 The two component automata#

Forbidden-pattern automaton.#

The orientation stream begins with the first edge orientation and continues with symbols q∈{0,1,2}q\in\{0,1,2\}. A suffix automaton retains enough orientation bits to decide every translated seven-edge signature when it closes. Deterministic-automaton minimization gives forty-eight accepting states and one dead state. Its transition table is h_table.hpp.

Grading transducer.#

For a support SS, the component term c⁢(PM2⁢[S])c(P_{M}^{2}[S]) starts a new component exactly when the new bit is one and the preceding two bits are zero. The odd-path term stores the last two triangle vertices, whether they lie in the same open interlace component, and the order parity of every component meeting the boundary. When a component leaves the boundary, the transducer emits one precisely when its order is odd. Exact minimization gives thirty-two reachable states. A transition emits a bit d∈{0,1}d\in\{0,1\}, and the total emitted sum, including a terminal flush, is νD⁢(S)\nu_{D}(S). Its table is grade_table.hpp.

S11.2 The coefficient automaton#

The external alphabet is

Σ={0,1,2}×{0,1}×ℳ,|Σ|=30.\Sigma=\{0,1,2\}\times\{0,1\}\times\mathcal{M},\qquad|\Sigma|=30. (S76)

A symbol (q,r,m)(q,r,m) supplies the next orientation insertion, the next bit of RR, and the next local quotient-basis symbol. The automaton nondeterministically chooses the next bit of XX. The bit of Y=X+RY=X+R is then fixed.

A raw state is the tuple

(h;c2,c1,d2,d1;X[−4],R[−4];m0,m1;gX,gY;eR,nR).(h;c_{2},c_{1},d_{2},d_{1};X_{[-4]},R_{[-4]};m_{0},m_{1};g_{X},g_{Y};e_{R},n_{% R}). (S77)

Here:

  • •

    hh is the forbidden-pattern DFA state;

  • •

    c2,c1,d2,d1c_{2},c_{1},d_{2},d_{1} are the orientation boundary bits;

  • •

    X[−4],R[−4]X_{[-4]},R_{[-4]} are four-bit histories, oldest first;

  • •

    m0,m1m_{0},m_{1} are the two basis symbols whose radius-two neighborhoods are not yet complete;

  • •

    gX,gYg_{X},g_{Y} are the two thirty-two-state grading states;

  • •

    eRe_{R} is the parity of edges already closed inside RR;

  • •

    nRn_{R} records whether noncentrality AM⁢R≠0A_{M}R\neq 0 has been witnessed.

When a new symbol and branch bit arrive, the site two positions behind is complete. The transition checks its row of table S1, advances both grading states, emits powers of z,wz,w, updates the appropriate sign parity, and shifts the boundary.

The first two sites are handled by 200=2⋅2⋅5⋅2⋅5200=2\cdot 2\cdot 5\cdot 2\cdot 5 external prefixes, each of which sums over the four choices of the initial XX-bits. At the right boundary, two zero sites are appended to close the pending local tests and flush the grading transducers. For commutation, a final state is accepted only if eR=1e_{R}=1. For inversion, it is accepted only if the noncentrality witness is present.

S11.3 Reachability and independent semantic audit#

Breadth-first closure gives

690,475⁢ reachable states,3,817,800⁢ transitions.690{,}475\text{ reachable states},\qquad 3{,}817{,}800\text{ transitions}. (S78)

The commutator has 5,8575{,}857 accepting states and 66,39466{,}394 states that can reach one. Inversion has 12,09212{,}092 accepting states and 69,87469{,}874 coaccessible states.

The state encoding was audited independently, and the full audit was rerun for this version. A separate program enumerates every HH-avoiding heap through M=9M=9, every external coefficient word encountered by the automaton, and every support branch. It compares:

  • •

    local compatibility with direct feasibility of XX and X+RX+R;

  • •

    transducer emissions with direct Gaussian elimination on KDK_{D};

  • •

    sign bits with direct graph-Clifford multiplication and y2y^{2}-reduction;

  • •

    e⁢(R)e(R) with direct induced-edge parity;

  • •

    the noncentrality flag with AM⁢RA_{M}R.

The audit covers 22,783,49822{,}783{,}498 branches with no discrepancy.

S11.4 Exact formal weighted bisimulation#

The raw automaton can be quotiented before choosing numerical values of z,wz,w. For a state ss, an input symbol aa, and a current partition block BB, aggregate all transitions

s→a,c⁢zp⁢wqt,t∈B,s\xrightarrow{a,\;cz^{p}w^{q}}t,\qquad t\in B,

by the tuple (a,B,p,q)(a,B,p,q), summing the integer coefficients cc. Two states are equivalent at the next refinement step when they have the same final weight and all such aggregated transition data agree. Iteration to stability is exact weighted bisimulation.

The resulting exact quotient sizes are

nC=9,756,nI=7,195.n_{\mathrm{C}}=9{,}756,\qquad n_{\mathrm{I}}=7{,}195. (S79)

The sparse quotients are stored in comm_formal.txt and inv_formal.txt. Their format is described in section S20.

For either quotient, let MaM_{a} be the transition matrix for a∈Σa\in\Sigma, let u1,…,u200u_{1},\ldots,u_{200} be the initial row vectors, and let ff be the final column. Every coefficient at every length is exactly

ui⁢Ma1⁢⋯⁢Mak⁢f.u_{i}M_{a_{1}}\cdots M_{a_{k}}f. (S80)

This is the standard linear representation of a noncommutative rational series [6].

S12 Exact invariant-module certificates#

The final step is a finite linear-algebra lemma.

Lemma S24 (Backward invariant-module criterion).

Let KK be a field, Ma∈Kn×nM_{a}\in K^{n\times n}, ui∈K1×nu_{i}\in K^{1\times n}, and f∈Kn×1f\in K^{n\times 1}. Suppose there is a subspace ℬ⊆Kn\mathcal{B}\subseteq K^{n} such that

f∈ℬ,Ma⁢ℬ⊆ℬ(a∈Σ),ui⁢b=0(i=1,…,200;b∈ℬ).f\in\mathcal{B},\qquad M_{a}\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{B}\quad(a\in\Sigma),% \qquad u_{i}b=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,200;\ b\in\mathcal{B}). (S81)

Then

ui⁢Ma1⁢⋯⁢Mak⁢f=0u_{i}M_{a_{1}}\cdots M_{a_{k}}f=0 (S82)

for every word and every initial row.

Proof.

By invariance, Ma1⁢⋯⁢Mak⁢f∈ℬM_{a_{1}}\cdots M_{a_{k}}f\in\mathcal{B}. Every uiu_{i} annihilates ℬ\mathcal{B}. ∎

S12.1 The two certificates#

For the commutator quotient, the supplied basis spans

ℬC⊆ℚ⁢(z,w)9756,dimℬC=590.\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{C}}\subseteq\mathbb{Q}(z,w)^{9756},\qquad\dim\mathcal{B}_% {\mathrm{C}}=590. (S83)

Its row-echelon encoding has 72,50572{,}505 nonzero entries and 1,4451{,}445 distinct rational functions. The exact verifier checks:

  1. 1.

    every one of the 200200 initial rows annihilates every basis vector;

  2. 2.

    the final column reduces to zero modulo the basis;

  3. 3.

    all

    590⋅30=17,700590\cdot 30=17{,}700 (S84)

For inversion, the certificate is

ℬI⊆ℚ⁢(z)7195,dimℬI=427.\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{I}}\subseteq\mathbb{Q}(z)^{7195},\qquad\dim\mathcal{B}_{% \mathrm{I}}=427. (S85)

427⋅30=12,810427\cdot 30=12{,}810 (S86)

The sparse bases were discovered by evaluating at generic points over 𝔽65521\mathbb{F}_{65521}, computing invariant spaces, and reconstructing rational functions from multiple evaluations. This discovery phase is not logically trusted. The verifier reads the reconstructed expressions into a characteristic-zero field and rechecks every condition in (S81). A wrong interpolation, modular collision, or corrupted candidate basis therefore causes an exact verification failure.

S12.2 Vanishing of all coefficients#

Apply lemma S24 to the two quotients. Equation (S80) vanishes for every input word and every length. By construction of the automata, this gives

CD,R,𝒎⁢(z,w)=0C_{D,R,\bm{m}}(z,w)=0 (S87)

for every HH-avoiding DD, every anticommuting RR, and every local basis word, and

ID,R,𝒎⁢(z)=0I_{D,R,\bm{m}}(z)=0 (S88)

for every noncentral RR. The coefficient sums are polynomials; their embeddings into the rational-function fields are injective, so rational-function vanishing is the desired formal polynomial identity.

We have proved commutation and centrality. Finally,

𝖠D⁢(z)⁢𝖠D⁢(−z)=𝖠D⁢(−z)⁢𝖠D⁢(z)=𝖠D⁢(z)⁢𝖠D⁢(−z)|z↦−z,\mathsf{A}_{D}(z)\mathsf{A}_{D}(-z)=\mathsf{A}_{D}(-z)\mathsf{A}_{D}(z)=\left.% \mathsf{A}_{D}(z)\mathsf{A}_{D}(-z)\right|_{z\mapsto-z},

so the central product is even in zz. It belongs to 𝒵M⁢[z2]\mathcal{Z}_{M}[z^{2}].

Proof of theorem 1.

If DD is HH-avoiding, theorem S14 gives the degree bound. The commutator certificate proves (S29), and the inversion certificate proves (S30). Thus DD has the canonical Baxter property. Conversely, a forbidden copy violates [QD,1,QD,3]=0[Q_{D,1},Q_{D,3}]=0 by corollary S13. ∎

S13 Analytic checks and special subclasses#

The computer-assisted proof is global, but several large subclasses and limiting cases have direct analytic explanations.

S13.1 Stable supports#

If SS is a stable set of PM2P_{M}^{2}, then ND,S=KD⁢(S)=0N_{D,S}=K_{D}(S)=0, independently of DD. Hence

νD⁢(S)=|S|.\nu_{D}(S)=|S|.

This recovers the ordinary independent-set grading of the original FFD transfer matrix. It also explains why deleting the diagonal of the footprint Gram matrix is essential: keeping the full Gram matrix would assign degree zero to every stable support.

S13.2 The three regular circuit families#

The half-words in (19) have periodic local orientations. In the edge order A⁢B,B⁢C,B⁢D,C⁢D,C⁢E,D⁢E,E⁢FAB,BC,BD,CD,CE,DE,EF, their translated six-site signatures are

Family Signatures, starting with a=1a=1
I 1111111
II 1011101, 1110111
III 0110001, 1000110, 1011101

The lists repeat with spatial periods one, two, and three. None is forbidden, proving acceptance at every compatible length. This check uses the same conventions as the scalar spectral constructions in Ref. [4]; no identification with a different transfer polynomial is required in the proof above.

S14 A constructive sector-aware inversion polynomial#

The classification theorem proves central inversion. This section gives an explicit scalar polynomial in every central sector, without an additional assumption that all sectors share the same polynomial. It also specifies the finite-frontier algorithm implemented in spectrum.py.

S14.1 The center has bounded dimension#

Let AMA_{M} be the binary adjacency matrix of PM2P_{M}^{2}. The monomial hR=h1R1⁢⋯⁢hMRMh^{R}=h_{1}^{R_{1}}\cdots h_{M}^{R_{M}} is central exactly when AM⁢R=0A_{M}R=0. With Rj=0R_{j}=0 outside [M][M], its components satisfy

Rj+2=Rj−2+Rj−1+Rj+1(mod2).R_{j+2}=R_{j-2}+R_{j-1}+R_{j+1}\pmod{2}. (S89)

The first boundary equation is R3=R2R_{3}=R_{2}. Thus R1,R2R_{1},R_{2} determine the entire vector; the right boundary can only impose further constraints. Consequently d:=dimker⁡AM≤2d:=\dim\ker A_{M}\leq 2 and there are at most four central support masks. The case M=1M=1 is immediate. Binary elimination gives both a kernel basis and the irreducible dimension 2(M−d)/22^{(M-d)/2}.

For a convenient real-coefficient bookkeeping convention, put

gS=i|S|⁢hS,bD⁢(S)=(−1)ιD⁢(S)⁢∏j∈Syj⁢∏j∉SeD⁢(j,S)=0xj,g_{S}=i^{|S|}h^{S},\qquad b_{D}(S)=(-1)^{\iota_{D}(S)}\prod_{j\in S}y_{j}\prod% _{\begin{subarray}{c}j\notin S\\ e_{D}(j,S)=0\end{subarray}}x_{j}, (S90)

where ιD⁢(S)\iota_{D}(S) counts reversed spatial edges in the selected temporal word. Then

𝖠D⁢(z)=∑S∈ℱ⁢(D)bD⁢(S)⁢zνD⁢(S)⁢gS,\mathsf{A}_{D}(z)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal{F}(D)}b_{D}(S)z^{\nu_{D}(S)}g_{S}, (S91)

and multiplication is

gS⁢gT=μ⁢(S,T)⁢gS⁢△⁢T,μ⁢(S,T)=(−1)|S∩T|+∑i>jSi⁢Tj⁢(AM)i⁢j.g_{S}g_{T}=\mu(S,T)g_{S\triangle T},\qquad\mu(S,T)=(-1)^{|S\cap T|+\sum_{i>j}S% _{i}T_{j}(A_{M})_{ij}}. (S92)

The first exponent comes from the powers of ii, and the second from restoring spatial order.

S14.2 Exact coefficient formula#

For every central support RR, define

pR⁢(z)=∑S,T∈ℱ⁢(D)T=S⁢△⁢RbD⁢(S)⁢bD⁢(T)⁢μ⁢(S,T)⁢(−1)νD⁢(T)⁢zνD⁢(S)+νD⁢(T).p_{R}(z)=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}S,T\in\mathcal{F}(D)\\ T=S\triangle R\end{subarray}}b_{D}(S)b_{D}(T)\mu(S,T)(-1)^{\nu_{D}(T)}z^{\nu_{% D}(S)+\nu_{D}(T)}. (S93)

The classification theorem gives the operator identity

𝖠D⁢(z)⁢𝖠D⁢(−z)=∑R∈ker⁡AMpR⁢(z)⁢gR.\mathsf{A}_{D}(z)\mathsf{A}_{D}(-z)=\sum_{R\in\ker A_{M}}p_{R}(z)g_{R}. (S94)

Consequently the required scalar polynomial is

pD,χ(z)=∑R∈ker⁡AMχ(gR)pR(z).\boxed{p_{D,\chi}(z)=\sum_{R\in\ker A_{M}}\chi(g_{R})p_{R}(z).} (S95)

This is a finite, explicit prescription for arbitrary admissible heaps. It requires no physical matrix representation.

To enumerate the central characters unambiguously, take a binary kernel basis R(1),…,R(d)R^{(1)},\ldots,R^{(d)} and let

pℓ=|R(ℓ)|+|E⁢(FM⁢[R(ℓ)])|(mod2),Cℓ=ipℓ⁢gR(ℓ).p_{\ell}=|R^{(\ell)}|+|E(F_{M}[R^{(\ell)}])|\pmod{2},\qquad C_{\ell}=i^{p_{% \ell}}g_{R^{(\ell)}}.

The CℓC_{\ell} are commuting Hermitian involutions. Choose χ⁢(Cℓ)=ζℓ∈{±1}\chi(C_{\ell})=\zeta_{\ell}\in\{\pm 1\} independently, set χ⁢(gR(ℓ))=i−pℓ⁢ζℓ\chi(g_{R^{(\ell)}})=i^{-p_{\ell}}\zeta_{\ell}, and use (S92) for every other radical mask. This avoids treating non-Hermitian central monomials as though their characters had to be real signs.

For R=0R=0, feasibility implies |E⁢(FM⁢[S])||E(F_{M}[S])| is even and νD⁢(S)≡|S|(mod2)\nu_{D}(S)\equiv|S|\pmod{2}. Therefore (S93) reduces to

p0⁢(z)=∑S∈ℱ⁢(D)z2⁢νD⁢(S)⁢∏j∈Syj2⁢∏j∉SeD⁢(j,S)=0xj2.p_{0}(z)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal{F}(D)}z^{2\nu_{D}(S)}\prod_{j\in S}y_{j}^{2}\prod_% {\begin{subarray}{c}j\notin S\\ e_{D}(j,S)=0\end{subarray}}x_{j}^{2}. (S96)

In the faithful Pauli representation this is the normalized full trace of the inversion product. A sector trace can also retain terms with R≠0R\neq 0. Thus (S96) alone is a sector polynomial only after scalar inversion in the full algebra has been proved or checked. No such extra claim is needed for (S95).

S14.3 Bounded-frontier evaluation#

Fix RR and scan the sites from left to right. At each site choose the bit SjS_{j}; then Tj=Sj+RjT_{j}=S_{j}+R_{j} is fixed. Two copies of the 32-state grading transducer accumulate νD⁢(S)\nu_{D}(S) and νD⁢(T)\nu_{D}(T). Two additional past bits of SS suffice for the radius-two feasibility and angle factors; the corresponding past bits of TT follow from RR. There are at most 4⋅322=40964\cdot 32^{2}=4096 frontier states. Each stores a polynomial of degree at most 2⁢sM2s_{M}.

Let Dj⁢k=1D_{jk}=1 when the spatial edge j−kj-k is directed from jj to kk. When site jj is finalized, the local angle factor is wj⁢(S)⁢wj⁢(T)w_{j}(S)w_{j}(T), where

wj⁢(S)={yj,Sj=1,xj,Sj=0,eD⁢(j,S)=0,1,Sj=0,eD⁢(j,S)=1.w_{j}(S)=\begin{cases}y_{j},&S_{j}=1,\\ x_{j},&S_{j}=0,\ e_{D}(j,S)=0,\\ 1,&S_{j}=0,\ e_{D}(j,S)=1.\end{cases}

Reject selected sites with odd outdegree parity in either support. Using νD⁢(T)≡|T|\nu_{D}(T)\equiv|T|, the sign emitted at that site is (−1)ηj(-1)^{\eta_{j}} with

ηj=Sj⁢Tj+Tj+∑k=max⁡(1,j−2)j−1[Dj⁢k⁢(Sk⁢Sj+Tk⁢Tj)+Sj⁢Tk](mod2).\eta_{j}=S_{j}T_{j}+T_{j}+\sum_{k=\max(1,j-2)}^{j-1}\left[D_{jk}(S_{k}S_{j}+T_% {k}T_{j})+S_{j}T_{k}\right]\pmod{2}. (S97)

The first two terms account for the gg-basis product and inversion parity; the sum accounts for the two temporal reorderings and the spatial product sign. Every spatial edge appears exactly once.

At initialization the degree already emitted by two bits (s1,s2)(s_{1},s_{2}) is s1∨s2s_{1}\lor s_{2}; add the analogous contribution for TT. Two zero-padding steps close the right boundary. The supplied implementation follows these conventions exactly. Polynomial coefficient vectors have 2⁢sM+12s_{M}+1 entries, so the arithmetic count is O⁢(M⁢sM)O(Ms_{M}) and the working storage is O⁢(sM)O(s_{M}), with fixed constants from the state bound. These are arithmetic-operation bounds, not bit-complexity or numerical-conditioning guarantees. The reference implementation uses floating arithmetic; its direct independent audit uses rational angle data for the underlying algebraic checks.

S15 Root selection, sign constraints, and physical quasienergies#

S15.1 Selecting one root from each pair#

For generic parameters let

pD,χ⁢(z)=a02⁢∏k=1sM(1−z2rχ,k2),a0≠0,p_{D,\chi}(z)=a_{0}^{2}\prod_{k=1}^{s_{M}}\left(1-\frac{z^{2}}{r_{\chi,k}^{2}}% \right),\qquad a_{0}\neq 0, (S98)

with distinct nonzero pairs. Any common transfer eigenvalue Λ⁢(z)\Lambda(z) satisfies Λ⁢(0)=a0\Lambda(0)=a_{0} and Λ⁢(z)⁢Λ⁢(−z)=pD,χ⁢(z)\Lambda(z)\Lambda(-z)=p_{D,\chi}(z). It must contain exactly one zero from each pair: neither omission nor double selection is compatible with a simple zero of pD,χp_{D,\chi}. Thus

Λχ,σ⁢(z)=a0⁢∏k=1sM(1+σk⁢zrχ,k).\Lambda_{\chi,\sigma}(z)=a_{0}\prod_{k=1}^{s_{M}}\left(1+\frac{\sigma_{k}z}{r_% {\chi,k}}\right). (S99)

This argument identifies the possible polynomials; completeness and multiplicities follow from the stable-set specialization in Theorem S11.

S15.2 The sign code is explicit for the open FFD chain#

Let I={1,4,7,…}∩[M]I=\{1,4,7,\ldots\}\cap[M], with |I|=sM|I|=s_{M}, and consider the commuting generators hjh_{j} on II. A vector supported on II lies in ker⁡AM\ker A_{M} only if its successive selected bits are all equal. The right boundary allows the nonzero constant vector precisely when M≡1(mod3)M\equiv 1\pmod{3}. Hence

dim(𝔽2I∩ker⁡AM)=δM:={1,M≡1(mod3),0,otherwise.\dim\bigl{(}\mathbb{F}_{2}^{I}\cap\ker A_{M}\bigr{)}=\delta_{M}:=\begin{cases}% 1,&M\equiv 1\pmod{3},\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases} (S100)

At the decoupled specialization, the sector therefore contains all 2sM2^{s_{M}} sign choices when δM=0\delta_{M}=0, and one parity half of them when δM=1\delta_{M}=1. Continuing the simple root pairs can only relabel coordinates or reverse their signs. The code remains either the full cube or a single product constraint; no more general binary code is needed for this chain.

When δM=1\delta_{M}=1, the highest charge QD,sMQ_{D,s_{M}} is central: its eigenvalue is the same for all allowed signs in each sector, and the identity extends polynomially from the generic locus. Write qχ,sM=χ⁢(QD,sM)q_{\chi,s_{M}}=\chi(Q_{D,s_{M}}). Comparing leading coefficients in (S99) fixes the sign constraint directly,

∏k=1sMσk=qχ,sMa0∏k=1sMrχ,k∈{±1}.\boxed{\prod_{k=1}^{s_{M}}\sigma_{k}=\frac{q_{\chi,s_{M}}}{a_{0}}\prod_{k=1}^{% s_{M}}r_{\chi,k}\ \in\{\pm 1\}.} (S101)

Its value depends on the chosen representatives of the root pairs. It is not legitimate to choose that parity independently of the sector.

The number of distinct generic transfer eigenpolynomials in one irreducible sector is 2sM−δM2^{s_{M}-\delta_{M}}. Each has multiplicity

2(M−d)/2−sM+δM.2^{(M-d)/2-s_{M}+\delta_{M}}. (S102)

A physical representation may contain additional copies of an irreducible sector. Special angles can merge distinct Floquet eigenvalues even when the transfer eigenpolynomials remain distinguishable.

S15.3 Reality of the physical root pairs#

For real angles, every transfer eigenpolynomial obeys

Λ⁢(z¯)¯=Λ⁢(−z).\overline{\Lambda(\bar{z})}=\Lambda(-z). (S103)

Suppose a root pair were not purely imaginary. Complex conjugation combined with z↦−zz\mapsto-z would either exchange the two members of that same pair, which contradicts one-root selection, or map it to a different pair. In the latter case the signs on those two pairs would have to be fixed multiples of one another in every allowed sign vector, by (S103). The full sign cube has no such relation. A single parity code also has no such two-coordinate relation when sM≥3s_{M}\geq 3. Thus all pairs are purely imaginary in these cases.

There is only one exceptional small code to check: M=4M=4, sM=2s_{M}=2, where the two signs in a fixed sector are correlated. Direct exact quotient-ring multiplication for all eighteen four-site heaps proves scalar inversion in the full algebra. The two sectors of the central product h1⁢h4h_{1}h_{4} then supply opposite parity halves of the same root polynomial, giving the full two-coordinate cube. The preceding argument applies to their union. The archive includes the all-angle four-site calculation (and checks at M=2,3,5M=2,3,5); it does not rely on a sampled-angle discriminant. When sM=1s_{M}=1, (S103) already makes the single nonzero root imaginary.

Therefore, on the generic real-angle locus, write rχ,k=i⁢uχ,kr_{\chi,k}=iu_{\chi,k}, uχ,k>0u_{\chi,k}>0. The normalized polynomial

PD,χ⁢(x)=pD,χ⁢(i⁢x)a02=∏k(1−xuχ,k2)P_{D,\chi}(x)=\frac{p_{D,\chi}(i\sqrt{x})}{a_{0}^{2}}=\prod_{k}\left(1-\frac{x% }{u_{\chi,k}^{2}}\right) (S104)

has positive roots. Unitarity at z=1z=1 gives pD,χ⁢(1)=1p_{D,\chi}(1)=1 and hence

a02⁢∏k(1+uχ,k−2)=1.a_{0}^{2}\prod_{k}(1+u_{\chi,k}^{-2})=1. (S105)

Substituting into (S99) yields the phase form

vχ,σ=sgn⁡(a0)⁢exp⁡[−i⁢∑kσk⁢arctan⁡(uχ,k−1)].v_{\chi,\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}(a_{0})\exp\!\left[-i\sum_{k}\sigma_{k}% \arctan(u_{\chi,k}^{-1})\right]. (S106)

This is the desired polynomial-roots-to-quasienergies solution, including the sector restriction rather than silently doubling its spectrum.

S15.4 Nongeneric points and numerical use#

The operator identities and unnormalized inversion polynomials hold for every angle. The factorization formulas using a0−1a_{0}^{-1}, simple roots, or distinct occupations require the generic assumptions explicitly stated above. At vanishing cosines or coalescing roots, take limits of the unnormalized identities. The supplied numerical solver does not discard small leading coefficients by an absolute trimming rule; near singular points or strongly separated root scales, higher-precision polynomial arithmetic and certified root isolation are preferable. A floating root computation is not an exact certificate for a spectrum.

S16 The twenty forbidden signatures#

Order the seven edges of HH as

(A⁢B,B⁢C,B⁢D,C⁢D,C⁢E,D⁢E,E⁢F),(AB,BC,BD,CD,CE,DE,EF),

and write a one when the first endpoint precedes the second. The twenty forbidden signatures are

0000010, 0001100, 0011000, 0011001, 0011101,\displaystyle 0000010,\ 0001100,\ 0011000,\ 0011001,\ 0011101,
0100000, 0100001, 0100011, 0110011, 0111101,\displaystyle 0100000,\ 0100001,\ 0100011,\ 0110011,\ 0111101,
1000010, 1001100, 1011100, 1011110, 1011111,\displaystyle 1000010,\ 1001100,\ 1011100,\ 1011110,\ 1011111,
1100010, 1100110, 1100111, 1110011, 1111101.\displaystyle 1100010,\ 1100110,\ 1100111,\ 1110011,\ 1111101.

They are generated from the five words in (S24) by temporal reversal and spatial reflection. The exact local verifier constructs this set independently and compares it with the nonzero commutator cases.

S17 Detailed sign derivation#

We record a direct derivation of lemma S22. Fix (D,R,𝒎)(D,R,\bm{m}), let Y=X+RY=X+R, and use the spatial normal order hS=h1S1⁢⋯⁢hMSMh^{S}=h_{1}^{S_{1}}\cdots h_{M}^{S_{M}}.

For a feasible support SS, write

HD⁢(S)=ηD⁢(S)⁢hS,ηD⁢(S)∈{±1}.H_{D}(S)=\eta_{D}(S)h^{S},\qquad\eta_{D}(S)\in\{\pm 1\}.

The product sign is

HD⁢(X)⁢HD⁢(Y)=ηD⁢(X)⁢ηD⁢(Y)⁢(−1)∑i>jXi⁢Yj⁢Ai⁢j⁢hR.H_{D}(X)H_{D}(Y)=\eta_{D}(X)\eta_{D}(Y)(-1)^{\sum_{i>j}X_{i}Y_{j}A_{ij}}h^{R}. (S107)

All powers of ii, all symbols fixed by (R,r,𝒎)(R,r,\bm{m}), and the sign at one base point may be factored out. The remaining dependence on XX is a binary affine character. One convenient representative is

χ⁢(X)=X𝖳⁢ED𝖳⁢R+𝟏Z𝖳⁢X,\chi(X)=X^{\mathsf{T}}E_{D}^{\mathsf{T}}R+\mathbf{1}_{Z}^{\mathsf{T}}X, (S108)

where ZZ is the subset of type-BB sites whose chosen local basis symbol is 11. The first term combines temporal and spatial normal-order signs; the second includes the local basis reduction.

Let Δ\Delta satisfy the homogeneous equations (S71). Since r=ED⁢Rr=E_{D}R,

χ⁢(X+Δ)−χ⁢(X)\displaystyle\chi(X+\Delta)-\chi(X) =Δ𝖳⁢ED𝖳⁢R+𝟏Z𝖳⁢Δ\displaystyle=\Delta^{\mathsf{T}}E_{D}^{\mathsf{T}}R+\mathbf{1}_{Z}^{\mathsf{T% }}\Delta
=∑v(ED⁢Δ)v⁢Rv+∑v∈ZΔv.\displaystyle=\sum_{v}(E_{D}\Delta)_{v}R_{v}+\sum_{v\in Z}\Delta_{v}. (S109)

At a type-AA site, (ED⁢Δ)v=0(E_{D}\Delta)_{v}=0. At a type-BB site, (ED⁢Δ)v=Δv(E_{D}\Delta)_{v}=\Delta_{v}. Type CC has Rv=0R_{v}=0 and Δv=0\Delta_{v}=0. The first sum therefore counts type-BB sites with Rv=1R_{v}=1, while ZZ counts the type-BB sites with Rv=0R_{v}=0. Together they give

χ⁢(X+Δ)−χ⁢(X)=∑v∈𝒯BΔv.\chi(X+\Delta)-\chi(X)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal{T}_{B}}\Delta_{v}.

Thus the commutator sign is a fixed constant times (−1)|𝒯B∩X|(-1)^{|\mathcal{T}_{B}\cap X|}.

For inversion, the summand has the additional factor (−1)νD⁢(Y)(-1)^{\nu_{D}(Y)}. Since νD⁢(Y)≡|Y|(mod2)\nu_{D}(Y)\equiv|Y|\pmod{2}, its ratio under X↦X+ΔX\mapsto X+\Delta is (−1)|Δ|(-1)^{|\Delta|}. Because Δ\Delta vanishes on type CC,

|𝒯B∩Δ|+|Δ|=|𝒯A∩Δ|(mod2).|\mathcal{T}_{B}\cap\Delta|+|\Delta|=|\mathcal{T}_{A}\cap\Delta|\pmod{2}.

This gives the inversion character.

S19 The grading transducer#

This appendix describes the finite state used to evaluate (S63). Retain the last two support bits to detect new components of PM2⁢[S]P_{M}^{2}[S]. For the triangle-interlace contribution, the boundary contains at most the last two triangle vertices. A raw interlace state records:

  • •

    whether each of the two vertices is present;

  • •

    if both are present, whether they belong to the same component;

  • •

    the order parity of every component that still meets the boundary.

Up to relabeling open components, the eleven possibilities are

(−,−),\displaystyle(-,-),
(−,0)0,(−,0)1,(0,−)0,(0,−)1,\displaystyle(-,0)_{0},\ (-,0)_{1},\quad(0,-)_{0},\ (0,-)_{1},
(0,0)0,(0,0)1,\displaystyle(0,0)_{0},\ (0,0)_{1},
(0,1)00,(0,1)01,(0,1)10,(0,1)11.\displaystyle(0,1)_{00},\ (0,1)_{01},\ (0,1)_{10},\ (0,1)_{11}.

When a new triangle vertex is introduced, its edges to the previous two vertices are known from the median rules. The update forms the corresponding union of boundary components and toggles the order parity of the component receiving the new vertex. Whenever a component no longer meets the boundary, the transducer emits its parity. The final flush emits the parities of all remaining components.

Combining these eleven states with the previous two support bits gives at most forty-four raw states. Removing unreachable states and minimizing the deterministic output transducer gives the thirty-two states stored in grade_table.hpp.

S20 Formal quotient file format#

The formal quotient files are sparse ASCII files. The first line contains

nnseed|Σ|.n\quad n_{\rm seed}\quad|\Sigma|.

The remaining lines have one of three forms:

F i ok s p q :fi=ok⁢(−1)s⁢zp⁢wq,\displaystyle:\quad f_{i}=\texttt{ok}\,(-1)^{s}z^{p}w^{q},
E src a dst p q c :(Ma)src,dst+=czpwq,\displaystyle:\quad(M_{a})_{\texttt{src},\texttt{dst}}\mathrel{+}=cz^{p}w^{q},
S i dst p q c :(ui)dst+=czpwq.\displaystyle:\quad(u_{i})_{\texttt{dst}}\mathrel{+}=cz^{p}w^{q}.

For inversion, every qq is zero. Integer coefficients with the same source, symbol, destination, and exponent pair have already been aggregated; zero totals are omitted.

S21 Certificate reconstruction and exact verification#

The discovery phase evaluates the formal quotient at several generic points over 𝔽65521\mathbb{F}_{65521}, computes a small backward invariant space, and records a stable pivot pattern. Coordinate functions are reconstructed as sparse rational functions. The commutator data contain 1,445 distinct functions, while inversion contains 330.

The exact verifier performs the following checks.

  1. 1.

    It constructs ℚ⁢(z,w)\mathbb{Q}(z,w) or ℚ⁢(z)\mathbb{Q}(z) using SymPy’s exact polynomial domains.

  2. 2.

    It reconstructs every basis entry and checks row-echelon normalization: pivot entries equal one and no entry lies left of its pivot.

  3. 3.

    It parses the formal quotient without numerical specialization.

  4. 4.

    For each basis vector and each seed, it computes the exact dot product and requires zero.

  5. 5.

    It reduces the exact final column by the basis and requires zero remainder.

  6. 6.

    For every basis vector bb and symbol aa, it forms Ma⁢bM_{a}b, performs sparse row reduction, and requires zero remainder.

The computations can be split into arbitrary index ranges. For this version, both complete ranges were independently rerun in a single pass, checking all 17,700 commutator images and all 12,810 inversion images.

S22 Pseudocode for the complete proof pipeline#

S23 Verification record and compact reproducibility bundle#

The accompanying ffd_certificate.pyz is a standard Python ZIP application containing the complete source files and certificate data. Its contents can be inspected with any ZIP reader or extracted with –extract DIRECTORY; it is not an opaque executable. The outer bundle contains only three files: this single LaTeX source, its PDF, and the code archive. A build and usage guide is included inside the archive. All figures and references are embedded in the LaTeX source.

S23.2 Independent checks of the constructive spectral route#

The new audit_new.py does not import the release’s support-expansion or nullity implementations. It constructs predecessor footprints directly and uses its own binary row reduction. For deterministic rational sine/cosine data, it compares the support expansion with a separate outside-in palindrome calculation and verifies the noncentral coefficients of the inversion product exactly. The same checks verify every fixed-support grading, the centrality of the highest charge when M≡1(mod3)M\equiv 1\pmod{3}, and the implemented sign constraints. Across 50 admissible permutations at 1≤M≤101\leq M\leq 10, the paired-frontier polynomial calculation agrees with the independent support-pair sum to at most 2.3×10−162.3\times 10^{-16} in the floating comparison.

For the irregular nine-site example in the letter, it separately constructs hj=Zj−2⁢Zj−1⁢Xjh_{j}=Z_{j-2}Z_{j-1}X_{j} on nine qubits (omitting factors outside the chain), multiplies the physical gates, and diagonalizes V=G⁢GTV=GG^{T}. The eight root-predicted eigenvalues each have multiplicity 64; the largest distance of an exact-matrix eigenvalue from the predicted set is 1.2×10−141.2\times 10^{-14}. This last comparison uses numerical linear algebra; it is a validation of the spectral implementation, not part of the symbolic theorem.

S23.3 Commands#

From the directory containing the code archive:

⬇
python ffd_certificate.pyz –quick
python ffd_certificate.pyz –full
python ffd_certificate.pyz –audit
python ffd_certificate.pyz –extract extracted_sources
python ffd_certificate.pyz –spectrum –example

The exact proof uses Python, SymPy, and a C++20 compiler. The numerical solver and independent dense audit additionally use NumPy. The archive contains the verification logs and machine-readable spectral audit. The archived README records the tested versions and gives the single-source PDF build command.
